name: NGC 4600 (Hubble)
blurb: NGC 4600, a dwarf lenticular galaxy, seen by Hubble.
label: ngc4600-hubble
story: NGC 4600 is a small, isolated lenticular galaxy with little gas, though a glow of hydrogen emission lingers in its core. Measuring its brightest red giant stars, Hubble placed it in front of the Virgo cluster rather than inside it.

claims.text: NGC 4600 is a gas-poor dwarf lenticular galaxy with H-alpha emission in the core
It is isolated and lies in front of the Virgo cluster
Distances measured from the tip of the red giant branch with Hubble's ACS
NGC 4600 is among the galaxies placed in front of Virgo
